newsitem.title: USA: Virus infections found to be a factor in asthma.
newsitem.headline: Virus infections found to be a factor in asthma.

text.p: Infections with certain common viruses can trigger the development of asthma and allergies, and vaccinations against the viruses could help prevent the diseases, according to a medical study released on Sunday.
Researchers said the study at Johns Hopkins University documents a long-suspected link between the viruses and asthma and allergies.

"This suggests we might one day be able to reduce the incidence of allergy and asthma by vaccinating children against mild childhood viral diseases that traditionally haven't received much attention," said study author Farhad Imani, an instructor of medicine at the university.
The study is to be presented at this week's annual meeting of the American Academy of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology, which began on Saturday and ends on Wednesday.

The test tube study on human cells showed that weak viral infections can make certain immune-system cells produce a type of protein, called immunoglobin E, that can cause allergies and many cases of asthma.

"We've suspected that there might be a connection since the late '70s, when studies found that kids who had more viral infections were more likely to have asthma and allergy later in life," Imani said in a release by the university.
The study found that stronger viruses capable of causing serious disease were less likely to trigger production of the immunoglobin E protein than weaker viruses.
